title: Terminal sections preserve epimorphisms over a separably closed field
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed]. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $T=(\operatorname{id}_S:S\to S)$ for the terminal object of its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The functor $F\mapsto F(T)$ from abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] to abelian groups preserves epimorphisms: every epimorphism $F\to G$ induces a surjection $F(T)\to G(T)$. This holds for all abelian sheaves, without a torsion or finite-generation hypothesis.

proof.text: This is the already proved library instance AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.preservesEpimorphisms_sheafSections_of_isSepClosed in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.PointCohomology. Its proof first shows that every covering sieve of the terminal object contains the identity: choose a nonempty covering member, then lift the unique point of Spec K along its etale map, using that K is separably closed. A sieve is downward closed, so this section puts the identity in the sieve. An epimorphism of abelian sheaves is locally surjective. Apply the identity-in-cover assertion to the image sieve of any terminal section to obtain its global lift. Surjectivity of an abelian-group homomorphism is equivalent to its being an epimorphism. The existing source declaration is used unchanged; no new Lean statement or open proof is introduced.
